source.title: Persistent learning signals and working memory without continuous attractors
source.authors: Il Memming Park; 'Abel S'agodi; Piotr Sok'ol

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares recurrent-network initializations and reports effects on learning sequence tasks, bearing on initialization and trainability. It does not test the listed claims about feedforward networks, CIFAR classification error, or the specific initialization recipes in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper reports benchmark outcomes for PTA-initialized RNNs. Results cited from prior work and theoretical examples are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests recurrent-network initialization for long-range sequence learning. V4 concerns initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth in plain feedforward networks; recurrence over time does not establish that claim. None of V1–V6 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that PTA initialization improves recurrent learning of long-range dependencies and report that training often removes initial oscillations. Their broader theoretical conclusion is that persistent memory alone does not ensure persistent learning signals, and they conjecture that PTA dynamics provide robust persistent temporal learning signals.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a block-structured rotation-matrix initialization for recurrent networks, compared with default and other recurrent baselines; tests long-range sequence tasks rather than the listed benchmark classification-error recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies by task: only PTA initialized networks reliably learned copy memory and sequential CIFAR, while on the other two benchmarks they learned faster and found better solutions.

fits_no_version.finding: PTA initialization improves long-range sequence learning in recurrent networks, with task- and architecture-dependent outcomes. Figure 5C reports faster convergence or better test performance; Section 2.8 additionally asserts reliable learning on sequential CIFAR without corresponding detailed results.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initializing recurrent networks with periodic toroidal attractor dynamics can improve learning of long-range temporal dependencies.

fits_no_version.finding: The theoretical analysis relates recurrent attractor topology and Lyapunov exponents to persistent temporal gradient signals, distinguishing persistent memory from persistent learning signals.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recurrent attractor dynamics determine whether temporal gradient signals persist; periodic attractors can support persistent signals robustly.

record.problems: The reported Table S1 is flattened and the PTA values cannot be confidently assigned; the qualitative training-curve descriptions do not give numeric estimates or uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: Table S1 numeric entries were not extracted because the flattened layout does not allow confident assignment of values to PTA initialization and task columns.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and size or training-recipe conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and the effects of extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation, identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh networks and Fixup.
Initialization-dependent speed and trainable depth in plain feedforward networks, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and deep convolutional kernels.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, catapult recovery and sharpness dynamics.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and normalization-free Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: The record inconsistently marks V4 as tested while linking every row to none. These recurrent-network results fit no supplied version. The cannot_determine states concern the supplied versions, not whether the paper reports benchmark improvements. Table S1 omissions were already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, or the stated size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Does not test two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems or spurious local minima.
Does not compare plain and residual convolutional networks across depth, or test Fixup and normalization conditions.

Tests PTA initialization in recurrent networks on sequence tasks, but not the listed activation-matched initializations, orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparison, or trainable depth of plain feedforward networks. Figure 5 reports qualitative comparisons; Table S1 is flattened such that PTA values cannot be confidently assigned.
Does not test learning rates above a stability limit or report sharpness dynamics.
Does not test batch normalization or Fixup.

rows.subject: PTA initialized RNNs
rows.operation_detail: Compared PTA initialization with other recurrent-model initializations on copy memory.
rows.measure: Learning task performance during training; test cross-entropy
rows.value: Only PTA initialized networks were able to reliably learn the task; figure shows performance curves.
rows.note: The paper does not provide a confidently assignable numeric PTA value in the flattened Table S1.
rows.check: A comparison of the proposed recurrent initialization with other methods, outside all versions. Its reported benefit is not evidence about feedforward trainable depth. Synthetic-task hidden-state size is 250; the measure is test cross-entropy, not training error.

rows.subject: PTA initialized RNNs
rows.operation_detail: Compared PTA initialization with other recurrent-model initializations on sequential CIFAR.
rows.measure: Learning task performance during training; test cross-entropy
rows.value: Only PTA initialized networks were able to reliably learn the task; figure shows performance curves.
rows.note: No CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification training-error result is reported.
rows.check: Section 2.8 explicitly mentions sequential CIFAR, but Figure 5C, supplementary task descriptions and Table S1 instead include random-delay copy memory and provide no sequential-CIFAR results. Retain only as a qualified textual assertion; its test-cross-entropy measure is not established. Recurrent sequential classification does not test V1 or V4.

rows.subject: PTA initialized RNNs
rows.operation_detail: Compared PTA initialization with other recurrent-model initializations on permuted sequential MNIST.
rows.value: PTA initialized RNNs learned faster and found better performing models.
rows.note: Qualitative result; the paper does not give a confidently assignable numeric PTA value in the flattened Table S1.
rows.check: The proposed recurrent method's benchmark performance falls outside all versions. Figure 5C reports test accuracy for this task, not both accuracy and cross-entropy. Section 2.8's reference to the other two benchmarks is ambiguous because its task list conflicts with the figure.

rows.subject: PTA initialized RNNs
rows.operation_detail: Compared PTA initialization with other recurrent-model initializations on temporal ordering.
rows.value: PTA initialized RNNs learned faster and found better performing models.
rows.note: The text groups temporal ordering with permuted seq-MNIST for this qualitative statement; no confidently assignable numeric PTA value is extracted.
rows.check: The proposed recurrent method's benchmark performance falls outside all versions. The measure is test cross-entropy; synthetic-task hidden-state size is 250. A grouped claim about PTA obscures architecture differences: Table S1 reports zero temporal-ordering loss for both default and PTA GRUs.
